dct_description_sm: The primary goal of the Arctic Network Dall's sheep monitoring program is to determine trends in the abundance and distribution of sheep in the parks and preserves which span the central and western Brooks Range, while being statistically robust enough to deal with the difficulties of surveying in this remote area. Over 41,000 km2 of potential Dall's sheep habitat have been delineated for this region, most of it within Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve (GAAR), Noatak National Preserve (NOAT), northern Kobuk Valley National Park (KOVA) and a small portion of Cape Krusenstern National Monument (CAKR). The region likely harbored 13-15% of the world's Dall's sheep population in the 1980s, followed by a precipitous decline in the early 1990s attributed to severe winter weather that likely reduced access to forage and increased vulnerability to predation.
